caption: Retired from service with United in 1934, this is the only surviving example of the Boeing Model 80 series. The airplane was later privately owned, barnstorming and conducting joy rides in the Pacific Northwest. It was also used as a flying electric billboard for night advertising in Southern California. In 1941, it became a cargo aircraft in Alaska. After the war, it was stored and then discarded. It was recovered from an Anchorage dump in 1960 and eventually brought to Seattle. The Model 80A-1 restoration project served as a catalyst for establishment of the Pacific Northwest Aviation Historical Foundation, which later became The Museum of Flight.
